title: The ICICI Bank – Videocon Loan Case
dek: A bank sanctioned crores in credit to a corporate group; CBI alleges the loan was linked to investments benefiting the bank CEO's husband. The prosecution's own arrest of the couple was later ruled illegal by the Bombay High Court.

heroStat.label: in credit facilities ICICI Bank sanctioned to the Videocon Group

promise.quote: Loan sanctions by ICICI Bank will be made on commercial merit, free of any personal financial benefit to the bank's decision-makers or their families.
promise.madeBy: ICICI Bank, under the leadership of then-CEO Chanda Kochhar
promise.role: Private sector bank; loan sanctioned under its internal credit approval process
promise.context: The CBI alleges ICICI Bank sanctioned ₹3,250 crore in credit facilities to the Videocon Group in 2012 in violation of lending norms, and that Videocon's chairman Venugopal Dhoot subsequently routed funds to NuPower Renewables, a company linked to Deepak Kochhar, husband of then-CEO Chanda Kochhar.

target.description: Credit sanctioned strictly on commercial merit through the bank's normal approval process, with no undisclosed personal financial interest for any decision-maker.
target.standard: RBI norms on related-party lending and conflict-of-interest disclosure for bank executives.

reality.description: The CBI registered a case on 24 January 2019 against Chanda Kochhar, Deepak Kochhar, and Videocon chairman Venugopal Dhoot, alleging the loan arrangement defrauded ICICI Bank. The CBI arrested Chanda and Deepak Kochhar in December 2022. In January 2023, the Bombay High Court ruled that the arrests had not followed mandatory legal procedure and granted the couple interim bail; a later bench confirmed that bail in February 2024.

gap.metricLabel: Credit sanctioned to Videocon vs. funds the CBI alleges were routed to a Kochhar-linked company
gap.actualDisplay: ₹64 cr allegedly routed to a Kochhar-linked entity
gap.note: The ₹64 crore figure is drawn from CBI allegations reported in the press, not from a court finding — no court has yet ruled on whether this routing occurred as alleged. A separate report describing a tribunal finding that Kochhar was 'held guilty' of a related bribery finding could not be clearly attributed to a specific proceeding by this investigation, and is not repeated here pending clearer sourcing.

legalStatus.summary: No trial verdict has been reached. Notably, the accused's own arrest was found procedurally illegal by the Bombay High Court, which is a setback for the prosecution rather than any finding on the underlying allegations.

verdict.summary: Preliminary verdict, pending fuller research: the loan sanction and the CBI's allegations are documented by the FIR and reputable reporting. What stands out procedurally is that the prosecution's own arrest of the accused was found unlawful by the High Court — a fact this investigation considers important context that is often missing from summary accounts of this case.
verdict.reasoning: This entry was added to establish the case's place in the site's timeline and its headline facts. A separate claim, that an appellate tribunal 'held Kochhar guilty' of a bribery finding, appeared in one source reviewed but could not be clearly attributed to a specific, identifiable proceeding, so it is not repeated here as fact.
